Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks — attached is our initial pass: commitment_scenarios_v2.pdf plus a filled workbook. High-level callouts below so your engineers and procurement have a short read:

Summary (TL;DR):
- GPU mix recommendation: A100-80GB for heavy-generation shards, A40 for embeddings-heavy nodes, and a small pool of L4s for lightweight scoring/reranks. This provides best cost/throughput balance for your mix.
- Baseline commitment: model the baseline on a 30-day rolling 95th percentile of steady-state sessions; we included three commitment scenarios (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with cost delta and burst runway.
- Burst mechanics: reserved pools support scheduled burst windows and an on-demand burst lane. Bursts are materialized from pre-warmed GPUs in a higher-cost tier; we can pre-sign up to 20% of committed capacity as burst credits for 6 months.
- Latency: We project p95 token-to-token at ~85ms for 256-token generations on A100-80GB under the Balanced scenario at 50 concurrent sessions. See page 3 of the PDF for the test matrix and assumptions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal review from your procurement on the three commitment scenarios.
2) Engineering to validate latency assumptions with a short acceptance run (we can provision a sandbox cluster for 48 hours).
3) If acceptable, we issue a pre-signed SLA and draft PO path for your legal.

I'll also loop in our pricing owner to make sure the delta for pre-signed bursts is explicit.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Naomi — thanks for the draft. A few engineering/pricing notes from my side:

Quick technical recommendations (for the decision matrix):
- Default group: 12 x A100-80GB for generation shards (balanced), 8 x A40 for embeddings, 4 x L4 for scoring.
- Hot-burst pool: 3 x A100-80GB reserved but tagged as burst-only; billed at a higher hourly run rate when used.
- KV-cache sizing: recommend 1.2TB NVMe per gen-shard to keep KV hit rates > 92% for your session patterns.

Pricing mechanics:
- Offer 12-month commitment with quarterly true-up; include 20% burst credits usable in any quarter (not cumulative).
- If procurement needs a 6-month pilot, we can provide a pilot discount tied to usage that converts to the full-year economics if they sign within 30 days of pilot end.

I attached a short note with the proposed GPU allocation table. I think the A40s give better net cost for embeddings than over-provisioning A100s.

Ben
Director of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Team — two operational flags from infra before we finalize the PDF:
1) Region alignment: Argus wants EU failover. If baseline is US, we must provision a shadow pool in eu-west-1 for their DR SLA. That changes egress and cross-region replication costs; modeled in scenario B.
2) On-prem constraints: for air-gapped installation we require a 4-week lead time for packaging and an additional security review. Private VPC is faster (~10 days) but we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration.

Operational ask: can procurement confirm whether they need EU failover in the initial commitment or as an add-on? If initial, we should present scenario costs in the workbook.

- Adi
